matches.rationale: No finding addresses the abstract's overgeneralized claim of consistent improvement with <1% parameters; all findings relate to method logic, experimental protocols, or citations elsewhere.
No finding identifies the inconsistency in the definition of the diagonal scaling matrix (unequal diagonal entries) versus later claims of equivalence to a uniform scalar.
No finding reports swapped or exaggerated accuracy values in Table 1; the findings about Section 5.1 discuss a different text/table discrepancy.
Both identify the uncontrolled training budget/compute discrepancy in the Section 5.2 pre-training comparisons that biases the evaluation and attributability of gains to HyperET.
No finding captures the misrepresentation of prior art in hyperbolic space learning in Section 2.3; the placeholder '[incorrect ref]' is a different corruption.
No finding discusses exaggerated gains or removed negative trends in Table 3 ablation results.
No finding addresses the rhetorical overstatement ('large margins', 'effectively bridges the granularity gap') in the Conclusion.
No finding mentions the omission of ethical risks, biases, or limitations in the Conclusion or Acknowledgment.
No finding discusses the unaddressed confusion between scalar equivalence and enhanced diagonal matrix flexibility in Sections 4.2/4.3.
Both identify the lack of critical experimental details (learning rate, batch size, steps, etc.) in the experimental setup, compromising reproducibility.
No finding reports the inflated accuracy gains in Table 4 across different vision encoders.
Both identify an algebraic error in the hyperbolic radius scaling theorem/derivation: the missing absolute value (|s|) or nonnegativity restriction on the learnable scalar s.
Both identify that the text mutes/downplays the necessity of Möbius multiplication while the actual results show a significant drop, obscuring an important ablation.
